quotes.speaker: JJ from the Sipp
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ from the Sipp on his comedy career and Dion Cole
quotes.excerpt: I just went ahead and stopped betting on myself. I just went ahead and stopped waiting around.
quotes.quote: When I heard about it, actually I was watching, I was in my yard. I was in my damn yard pulling weeds. I already loved the show and me and Dion Cole, we started back in the trenches a long time ago. So when I found out the episode was on, I just had it on, man. Just in the yard. Then he said who his favorite was, man. I ain't pulling not one other weed that day. I just went ahead and stopped betting on myself. I just went ahead and stopped waiting around, figuring out shit, letting somebody else figure out what I want to do with my own career. So I just got in them trenches on my own, man, investing my own money. Me and my team put our heads together, man, and we put out a masterpiece.

quotes.speaker: JJ from the Sipp
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ from the Sipp on building his comedy career
quotes.excerpt: I'm not new. I've been in the trenches, man. I'm trying to still figure out my way.
quotes.quote: I'm just going to keep this and ride this train, man, keep this going, man, continue to put it out there like it just started, like I just dropped it. Keep pushing on our name, man, come up with some creative ideas on my social media, man, just building that foundation, man, let these folks know, hey, I'm not new. I've been in the trenches, man. I'm trying to still figure out my way, my niche into the business, man, and just went on ahead and stopped betting on myself. You not stop waiting around, figuring out shit, you know, let somebody else figure out what I want to do with my own career, man. So I just got in them trenches on my own, man, investing my own money. Me and my team put our heads together, man, and we put out a masterpiece.

quotes.speaker: JJ from the Sipp
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ from the Sipp on taking comedy seriously
quotes.excerpt: I took comedy serious back in 1995. This is when I first started, man.
quotes.quote: I took comedy serious back in 1995. This is when I first started, man. I always wanted to be in the comedy business, but I was negative about it, being from Mississippi, like, man, who going to discover this dude right here, man? Ain't nobody going to be looking for nobody from the Sipp, man. So I put it almost like in a box and threw away the key. I never told nobody I wanted to be in the entertainment business. Like I probably didn't even talk to God about it, but I know He knew my path and never even just mentioned it to Him, man. So moving to the ATL out of college, man, just making some buddies laugh out the blue, man, just messing around, blazing and drinking New Year's Eve, man, and making some people laugh, you know, nothing, just having fun.

quotes.speaker: JJ from the Sipp
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ from the Sipp on Steve Harvey's influence
quotes.excerpt: Steve Harvey sparked the interest because I had stopped college for a minute, man, just was mentally drained.
quotes.quote: Steve Harvey sparked the interest because I had stopped college for a minute, man, just was mentally drained. Moved to Dallas, man, I was going to a little space, space and bingo night on Thursdays, man. And after that, man, you know, Steve Harvey would come out and do comedy shows, man, and I mean shows and stuff, man, you know, the light bulb, you know, it sparked. But you know, never just pursued it at that time, man. So Steve Harvey was definitely one, man, you know, all the Kings, man. Then I was blessed to you know, ride out with Cedric the Entertainer for about 12 years, you know, learn the game, build my brand, build my, you know, my fan base throughout, you know, his thing because that was just right after the Kings of Comedy. And he was hot, so everybody went their separate ways and Cedric was like, hey man, ride with me, man. Let me teach you another level of the business, man, because I see something in you.

quotes.speaker: JJ from the Sipp
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ from the Sipp on Mississippi's water crisis
quotes.excerpt: We been hearing about the hanging, you know, the water system down there is real bad, man.
quotes.quote: Me and my family, man, you know, I got a lot of relatives down there, my brothers and sisters down there, man, you know, we been putting our heads together right now, man, you know, we been doing a lot of zooms with my brothers and sisters and cousins, man. We were talking about the family reunion, man, but you know, we been hearing about the hanging, you know, the water system down there is real bad, man. I been noticing now, man, that our prison down there is just doing terrible, Parchman prison down there, man. So, you know, we trying to figure it out to be real, man. We just putting all our resources together, man. We reaching out to any powerful sources that we know in the Sipp or surrounding areas, man, that will come down, you know, and just, you know, help us, you know, guide us in the right direction, man.

quotes.speaker: JJ from the Sipp
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ from the Sipp on the current state of comedy
quotes.excerpt: I don't want nobody to forget the essence of comedy, man. It's about them jokes.
quotes.quote: I wish we can go back, you know, I don't want nobody to forget the essence of comedy, man. It's about them jokes, making folks laugh, man, you know, I'm and you know, we in a different times, man. So, you know, crowd work is is amazing, um, you know, social media is amazing, but you know, I want y'all, I mean, the folks that are trying to be real comedians, don't forget about, you know, what they paved the way for where we are now, man. You know, man, there's a lot of people put their blood, sweat and tears and take comedy serious. I want everybody that really want to call themselves comedians, man, take it serious. You know, don't don't look for that quick fame and it's cool. Hey, that's what we are. It is what it is. But you know, don't call yourself a real comedian, man, and you ain't put the work in.

quotes.speaker: JJ from the Sipp
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ from the Sipp on underrated comedians
quotes.excerpt: It's a lot of them, man, you know, I enjoy the underground comedy scene, man.
quotes.quote: It's a lot of them, man, you know, I enjoy the underground comedy scene, man, you know, folks that just didn't have that opportunity like myself, man. Uh, man, it's a just niche out there. She's a very, very funny sister, Jess Hilarious is out there. Ken Henry Coleman, uh, he's out there rocking very well, man. I got a cat that goes on the road with me named Lamar Jones, Cameron Keys, man, I'm it's a lot of them, Steve Brown, man, you know, the list goes, Darius Bradford, man, I mean, it's some really funny cats out there that I'm fortunate, man, the exposure is not like it used to be, man. You know, I came in the tail end of Def Jam and I did it. I did it twice and I did ComicView a few times, man, but it wasn't like it was, you know, back in the day, man.
